chunks: From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from one of the two عليهمَا السَّلَامُ, who said:

I said: A man entered a thicket in which there is no water, but there is mud; what should he do? He said, «He performs tayammum, for it is sa'id.» I said: But he is mounted and cannot dismount out of fear, and he is not in a state of wudu (ablution). He said, «If he fears for himself from a beast or something else, and he fears the passing of the time, then let him perform tayammum: he strikes with his hand upon the felt and the pack-saddle, performs tayammum, and offers salat (prayer).»

key_terms.الصَّعِيدُ: earthy ground or surface used for tayammum
key_terms.اللِّبْدِ: felt or thick cloth placed on the mount
key_terms.الْأَجَمَةَ: a thicket or marshy wooded place
key_terms.الْبَرْذَعَةِ: the pack-saddle or saddlecloth on the riding animal
key_terms.سَبُعٍ: a predatory beast or dangerous animal
key_terms.طِينٌ: mud present in place of accessible water
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, the dry ablution

ai.seo_question: What should a person do for tayammum if there is no water and getting down from a mount is dangerous?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling of tayammum when water is unavailable and mud is present, treating such earth-derived matter as valid for purification. It also addresses a case of danger and urgency, permitting tayammum from materials on a riding animal when dismounting is unsafe and the prayer time may expire.
